source_title: Casper Sleep Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement
publisher_issuer: Casper Sleep Inc., filed with U.S. SEC (EDGAR CIK 0001598674)
company_context: Casper Sleep is a direct-to-consumer mattress and sleep-products company that filed its S-1 in January 2020 ahead of its February 2020 IPO. The filing showed strong revenue growth alongside persistent net losses, the classic DTC margin/unit-economics tension.
business_type: DTC consumer products startup (online mattress / sleep brand)
evidence_summary: Casper grew net revenue from $169.1 million (2016) to $250.9 million (2017) to $357.9 million (2018), a 45.5% CAGR, but lost $73.4 million in 2017 and $92.1 million in 2018. Gross margin expanded from 42.8% (2016) to 44.1% (2018) and to 50.7% for the three months ended September 30, 2019, yet high marketing and operating costs kept the company unprofitable - the hallmark thin-margin DTC unit-economics problem where heavy customer-acquisition spend outpaces contribution.
outcome_evidence: S-1 disclosed widening absolute net losses ($73.4M in 2017 to $92.1M in 2018) despite ~45.5% revenue CAGR and improving gross margin. Casper IPO'd in February 2020 at a sharply reduced valuation; the filing is the primary evidence of growth-with-hidden-profitability-problem.
source_limitations: The SEC EDGAR S-1 document returned 403 to direct WebFetch here, but the cited URL is the verified primary EDGAR filing location surfaced by search; figures were confirmed verbatim via WebSearch snippets quoting the S-1. The 2020 full-year net loss figure ($89.6M) referenced elsewhere is post-S-1 and not part of this filing.
inferred: Customer-acquisition and operating spend, not gross margin alone, drove losses
Revenue growth alone did not establish a path to profitability
why_useful_for_opsiq: Clean DTC unit_economics_failure / thin-margin case from a primary SEC filing. Tests whether a system separates improving gross margin from overall unprofitability and recognizes that growth plus margin expansion can still mask a non-viable cost structure.
